legend: Vasya has got a robot which is situated on an infinite Cartesian plane, initially in the cell (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$. Robot can perform the following four kinds of operations:
Vasya also has got a sequence of n$$$n$$$ operations. Vasya wants to modify this sequence so after performing it the robot will end up in (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$.

Vasya wants to change the sequence so the length of changed subsegment is minimum possible. This length can be calculated as follows: maxID−minID+1$$$maxID - minID + 1$$$, where maxID$$$maxID$$$ is the maximum index of a changed operation, and minID$$$minID$$$ is the minimum index of a changed operation. For example, if Vasya changes RRRRRRR to RLRRLRL, then the operations with indices 2$$$2$$$, 5$$$5$$$ and 7$$$7$$$ are changed, so the length of changed subsegment is 7−2+1=6$$$7 - 2 + 1 = 6$$$. Another example: if Vasya changes DDDD to DDRD, then the length of changed subsegment is 1$$$1$$$.

If there are no changes, then the length of changed subsegment is 0$$$0$$$. Changing an operation means replacing it with some operation (possibly the same); Vasya can't insert new operations into the sequence or remove them.
Help Vasya! Tell him the minimum length of subsegment that he needs to change so that the robot will go from (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$ to (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$, or tell him that it's impossible.
input: The first line contains one integer number n (1≤n≤2⋅105)$$$n~(1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5)$$$ — the number of operations.
The second line contains the sequence of operations — a string of n$$$n$$$ characters. Each character is either U, D, L or R.
The third line contains two integers x,y (−109≤x,y≤109)$$$x, y~(-10^9 \le x, y \le 10^9)$$$ — the coordinates of the cell where the robot should end its path.
output: Print one integer — the minimum possible length of subsegment that can be changed so the resulting sequence of operations moves the robot from (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$ to (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$. If this change is impossible, print −1$$$-1$$$.
note: In the first example the sequence can be changed to LULUU. So the length of the changed subsegment is 3−1+1=3$$$3 - 1 + 1 = 3$$$.
In the second example the given sequence already leads the robot to (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$, so the length of the changed subsegment is 0$$$0$$$.
In the third example the robot can't end his path in the cell (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$.

legend.ai: Vasya 有一个机器人，机器人位于无限大的笛卡尔平面上，初始位于单元格 (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$。机器人可以执行以下四种操作：
Vasya 还有一个包含 n$$$n$$$ 个操作的序列。Vasya 想要修改这个序列，使得执行完这些操作后机器人最终停在 (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$。

Vasya 想要修改序列，使得被修改子段的长度尽可能小。这个长度可以按如下方式计算：maxID−minID+1$$$maxID - minID + 1$$$，其中 maxID$$$maxID$$$ 是被修改操作的最大下标，minID$$$minID$$$ 是被修改操作的最小下标。例如，如果 Vasya 把 RRRRRRR 改成 RLRRLRL，那么下标为 2$$$2$$$、5$$$5$$$ 和 7$$$7$$$ 的操作被修改，因此被修改子段的长度为 7−2+1=6$$$7 - 2 + 1 = 6$$$。另一个例子：如果 Vasya 把 DDDD 改成 DDRD，那么被修改子段的长度为 1$$$1$$$。
如果没有修改，那么被修改子段的长度为 0$$$0$$$。修改一个操作是指把它替换为某个操作(可能与原来相同)；Vasya 不能向序列中插入新操作，也不能删除操作。
帮帮 Vasya！告诉他需要修改的子段的最小长度，使得机器人能从 (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$ 到达 (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$，或者告诉他这是不可能的。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n (1≤n≤2⋅105)$$$n~(1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5)$$$ — 操作的数量。
第二行包含操作序列，即一个长度为 n$$$n$$$ 的字符串。每个字符均为 U、D、L 或 R。
第三行包含两个整数 x,y(−109≤x,y≤109)$$$x, y~(-10^9 \le x, y \le 10^9)$$$，表示机器人应结束路径的单元格坐标。

output.ai: 输出一个整数，即为使操作序列发生改变后，机器人从 (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$ 移动到 (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$，所需改变的子段的最小可能长度。如果无法完成改变，输出 −1$$$-1$$$。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，可以将序列改变为 LULUU。因此，改变的子段长度为 3−1+1=3$$$3 - 1 + 1 = 3$$$。
在第二个样例中，给定的序列已经可以使机器人到达 (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$，因此改变的子段长度为 0$$$0$$$。
在第三个样例中，机器人无法在单元格 (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$ 结束路径。
